questions.prompt: The phishing message passed SPF. What does that tell you about the sender?
options: The message was legitimate and from the claimed sender
Only that the attacker's own domain authorized their own sending server -- SPF validates the Return-Path domain, not the From header
That DKIM must also have passed
That DMARC was set to reject
questions.explanation: An attacker with a correctly configured domain passes SPF trivially. DMARC was present but set to p=none, so the alignment failure did not block delivery.

questions.prompt: Event ID 4662 with replication GUIDs fired correctly during the DCSync. Why did it not prevent the compromise?
options: The event was suppressed by the attacker
The telemetry existed but no detection rule consumed it -- the 'telemetry, no detection' coverage level
Directory Service Access auditing was disabled
questions.explanation: This is the gap an honest coverage map exposes: collecting the data and detecting on it are different capabilities, and only the second changes outcomes.

questions.prompt: Why was the staged krbtgt reset chosen over rapid succession?
options: Rapid succession does not actually work
No evidence of active destruction existed, and domain-wide authentication disruption during month-end close was judged worse than ten more hours of an already eight-day-old Golden Ticket
The forest had too many domain controllers
questions.explanation: The choice is an incident-command decision weighing disruption against exposure, made explicitly rather than by default.

questions.prompt: What did the initial remediation plan miss, and why did it matter?
options: The scheduled task, which would have re-run at logon
The additional credential on an existing app registration -- the attacker would have retained tenant access through a complete on-premises rebuild
The LSASS dump file in C:\Windows\Temp
questions.explanation: Cloud persistence survives on-premises remediation entirely, which is why the coordinated remediation event must include app registrations and certificates alongside credentials.
